tokens.intro: API tokens are for mobile apps, scripts, CLIs and AI agents (MCP). Send the token in the {{header}} header.
tokens.introHint: Issue a separate token for each client and grant only the rights it needs — then you can revoke it without affecting the others.
tokens.emptyText: Create a token to connect a script, an app or an AI agent.

confirm.deleteMessage: All clients using the token {{name}} will lose access immediately. This can't be undone.

dialog.fullHint: Read and write access to every section, including those added in future panel versions.
dialog.readonlyHint: Read access to every section except commands/terminal and API tokens. Nothing can be changed — good for monitoring and dashboards.
dialog.emptyInfo: A token without rights can only check itself (/auth/me) and connect to MCP with no tools.

created.title: Token created
created.warning: Copy the token now — it's shown only once. After that you can only revoke it and issue a new one.

reference.specInfo: OpenAPI {{version}} · {{endpoints}}. Use the spec to generate a client for a mobile app or service — openapi-generator, swift-openapi-generator, orval, openapi-typescript, etc.
reference.overviewHint: Pick an endpoint on the left to see its parameters and schemas and to send a request.
reference.rawBody: Raw file bytes (up to the server limit), no JSON wrapper.
reference.wsInfo: This is a WebSocket — it can't be called from the reference. Connect with a WebSocket client (in a browser — with the session cookie, otherwise pass the token in the token parameter):
reference.binaryInfo: The body is raw file bytes, so the request can't be sent from here. Use the curl below with --data-binary.
reference.downloadInfo: The response is a file. Open the link (works with your session) or use the curl below.
reference.liveNote: The request is executed for real, with your session's rights (full access).

mcp.intro: MCP is an open protocol that gives AI agents (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and others) a set of “tools” they call on their own. NodePilot exposes its features as an MCP server: an agent can view stats, run commands, edit files, keep notes and graphs — within the token's rights.
mcp.stdioHint: on the machine running the panel
mcp.scopeInfo: An agent sees only the tools its token allows: a “Read-only” token won't expose any tool that changes data. Create a separate token for the agent on the Tokens tab and use it in place of np_….
